caption_en:
The first one took 11 minutes. The rest is still being counted.

14 May 1948: Israel's leaders sign the Declaration of Independence in Tel Aviv. At midnight Tel Aviv time (6 pm in Washington) the British Mandate ends and the state is born. 11 minutes later, the United States recognises it (de facto). 17 May 1948: the Soviet Union gives the first full legal (de jure) recognition.

End of 1948: 17 countries. By 1950: 47. The 1960s: dozens of newly independent African states. 1979: Egypt, the first Arab country. The 1990s: about 40 more as the Soviet Union breaks up, including China (1992) and Jordan (1994). 2020: the UAE, Bahrain and Morocco (and Bhutan).

Today: 169 of the other 192 UN members. 23 do not: Afghanistan, Algeria, Bangladesh, Brunei, Comoros, Djibouti, Indonesia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, North Korea, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, Yemen. These are governments' decisions, not peoples'.

Recognising is not agreeing: many of them criticise Israel too, and some have cut ties and restored them over the years.

Which one surprised you?

Sources: US National Archives, "U.S. Recognition of the State of Israel" (11 minutes); Wikipedia, International recognition of Israel (Feb 2026). Photos: Eliezer Kaplan signs the Declaration, 1948, Zoltan Kluger, GPO (PD); Eliahu Epstein's letter to President Truman, 14 May 1948, Truman Library (PD); Sadat, Carter and Begin at the Camp David Accords, 1978, the road to the 1979 treaty (PD); Abraham Accords signing, 2020, White House (PD). Map: Natural Earth (PD). Made with AI tools, AI voice (Noam's cloned voice), follow line in Noam's own voice.
caption_he:
מי הכיר בישראל ראשונה? ארצות הברית, 11 דקות אחרי שהמדינה קמה (הכרה בפועל). שלושה ימים אחר כך, ברית המועצות נתנה את ההכרה המשפטית המלאה הראשונה.
סוף 1948: 17 מדינות. 1950: 47. 1979: מצרים, המדינה הערבית הראשונה. שנות ה 90: עוד כ 40, כולל סין וירדן. 2020: איחוד האמירויות, בחריין ומרוקו.
היום: 169 מתוך 192 חברות האו"ם האחרות. 23 עדיין לא מכירות. הכרה היא לא הסכמה.

lines.line: May fourteenth, 1948. In Tel Aviv, Israel's leaders sign the Declaration of Independence.
At midnight in Tel Aviv, six in the evening in Washington, the new state is born.
Eleven minutes later, President Truman recognises it.
The United States is first. In practice, not yet in law.
Three days later, the Soviet Union gives the first full legal recognition.
By the end of 1948, seventeen countries. By 1950, forty seven.
The nineties: forty more, including China and Jordan.
Today: one hundred sixty nine of the other one hundred ninety two United Nations members.
Recognising isn't agreeing. Many of them still criticise Israel.
If you love Israeli facts, follow Noam Roz for more.
The first took eleven minutes. Twenty three still haven't, seventy eight years later.
